Question.content: Estimate the second quartile (Q₂) (median) from the given frequency distribution, correcting your answer to 2 decimal places.

Explanation.content:
Estimating the Median (Second Quartile) from a Grouped Frequency Distribution

Key Concept
The median (or second quartile, \( Q_2 \)) is the middle value in a dataset when arranged in order. For grouped frequency distributions, the median is estimated using the formula:
\[ Q_2 = L + \left( \frac{\frac{N}{2} - CF}{f} \right) \times w \]
Where:
\( L \) = Lower boundary of the median class
\( N \) = Total frequency
\( CF \) = Cumulative frequency of the class immediately preceding the median class
\( f \) = Frequency of the median class
\( w \) = Class width
Given
Frequency distribution table:
| Class interval | Frequency (f) |
| :------------- | :------------ |
| 140 – 150 | 6 |
| 150 – 160 | 16 |
| 160 – 170 | 21 |
| 170 – 180 | 8 |
Estimate the second quartile (median) to 2 decimal places.

Step 1: Calculate the total frequency (N)
Sum all the frequencies to find the total number of observations, \( N \).
\[ N = 6 + 16 + 21 + 8 \]
\[ N = \text{51} \]

Step 2: Determine the position of the median
The median position is found by dividing the total frequency by 2.
\[ \text{Median Position} = \frac{N}{2} \]
\[ \text{Median Position} = \frac{51}{2} \]
\[ \text{Median Position} = \text{25.5} \]

Step 3: Construct the cumulative frequency table and identify the median class
Create a cumulative frequency column to find the class interval where the 25.5th observation lies.
| Class interval | Frequency (f) | Cumulative Frequency (CF) |
| :------------- | :------------ | :------------------------ |
| 140 – 150 | 6 | 6 |
| 150 – 160 | 16 | 6 + 16 = 22 |
| 160 – 170 | 21 | 22 + 21 = 43 |
| 170 – 180 | 8 | 43 + 8 = 51 |
The 25.5th observation falls within the class where the cumulative frequency first exceeds 25.5. This is the 160 – 170 class interval.

Step 4: Identify the values for the median formula
From the median class (160 – 170) and the cumulative frequency table, identify the necessary values:
\( L \) (Lower boundary of the median class) = 160
\( CF \) (Cumulative frequency of the class before the median class) = 22
\( f \) (Frequency of the median class) = 21
\( w \) (Class width) = \( 150 - 140 = \text{10} \)

Step 5: Apply the median formula
Substitute the identified values into the median formula:
\[ Q_2 = L + \left( \frac{\frac{N}{2} - CF}{f} \right) \times w \]
\[ Q_2 = 160 + \left( \frac{25.5 - 22}{21} \right) \times 10 \]
\[ Q_2 = 160 + \left( \frac{3.5}{21} \right) \times 10 \]
\[ Q_2 = 160 + (0.166666... ) \times 10 \]
\[ Q_2 = 160 + 1.666666... \]
\[ Q_2 = \text{161.666666...} \]

Step 6: Round the answer to 2 decimal places
Rounding the calculated median to two decimal places:
\[ Q_2 \approx \text{161.67} \]

Verification
The median class is 160 – 170. Our calculated median, 161.67, falls within this class interval, which is consistent with the definition of the median class.

∴ The second quartile (median) is 161.67
